narrative: Material PL1__M9491162 exhibits moderate demand volatility (CV=17.2%) with a statistically significant downward trend over the observation window (Mar 2025–Mar 2026). Lead times cluster around 4–5 working days but show meaningful variability (CV~30%), with one observation as high as 7.29 days. The current SAP safety stock of 0 provides no buffer against this combined demand and lead-time uncertainty, creating meaningful stockout exposure. The recommended (r,Q) policy with SS=10,886 and OQ=71,635 units corrects this gap, reduces annual order frequency from 42.5 to 16.7 cycles, and delivers a net 21.6% cost reduction while staying well within the 114,631-unit storage capacity.

Order quantity increased from EOQ 55,285 to MOQ 71,635 — holding cost elevated relative to pure EOQ optimum

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is continuous and arrives daily on working days; lead times are variable but not extreme. The MOQ of 28,149 units provides a natural lower bound that aligns with the fixed-Q structure. The EOQ formula identifies the cost-optimal quantity (55,285), which is below the MOQ, so the MOQ of 71,635 (next MOQ multiple above EOQ) becomes the operative order quantity. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy minimizes total inventory cost under these conditions without requiring periodic-review complexity.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Order quantity is driven to 71,635 by the MOQ constraint rather than pure EOQ (55,285). This inflates holding costs by approximately 30% above the unconstrained optimum. Storage utilization post-replenishment reaches ~72% (82,521 / 114,632 units), leaving an adequate ~31,000-unit buffer. If safety stock were to grow (e.g. due to increased lead-time variance), the effective capacity headroom would shrink and should be monitored.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ + safety_stock (82,521) is below max_storage_units (114,632); no infeasibility
